title: P1 keeps a lake copy after the data lake is removed
source: TSD P1 v3 (T1, T2, T3.1 lake_copy_watermark) against Architecture v5 and DP-17
description: TSD P1 v3 keeps the decision log copy to the data lake and the lake_copy_watermark table. Architecture v5 (ADR-018) and DP-17 remove the data lake, and rwb-reporting reads events instead.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 lists lake_copy_watermark as a P1 table; ADR-018 and Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 remove the data lake; TSD P1 v3 T1 keeps 'the decision log copy to the data lake'.
proposed: Keep lake_copy_watermark as the watermark of the last published reporting projection and drop the lake extract INT-19 and INT-20 (DP-17).

title: TSD P2 names platform tables and one P1 table as its own
source: TSD P2 v3 T3.1 against Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet
description: T3.1 of TSD P2 lists outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, idempotency_key, feature_flag and feature_flag_change, which are shared-library tables, and efs_ledger_outcome, which the Ownership Map places with P1. The map has three P2 business tables only.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables sheet: interface_config, job_catalog and outbound_item for P2; Architecture v5 slide 41 the same three; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 lists ten objects.
proposed: Build the platform tables once in the shared libraries (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON) and keep efs_ledger_outcome with P1.

title: The rule package registry is claimed by P3 and P4 as well as P7
source: TSD P3 v3 T2.2 and T3.1; TSD P4 v3 T1, T2, T3.1 against Architecture v5 slide 41 and the Ownership Map
description: TSD P3 v3 names rule_test_case as 'owned by P4', and TSD P4 v3 owns rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the DMN model registry to rwb-decision and the Ownership Map gives all four tables to P7.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 (P7 owns 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'); Ownership Map Tables sheet: rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case under P7.
proposed: Build the registry in rwb-decision, keep embedded Drools evaluation in the owning service, and read the package and catalogue through the P7 contract (DP-04).

title: payment_match_rule has no owner in the Ownership Map
source: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 against Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet
description: T3.1 of TSD P8 defines payment_match_rule as a NEW table. The Ownership Map has no row for it and gives P8 the proceeds table only. The match rules are a decision table, and Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04 and ADR-017 put every rule in the registry of rwb-decision.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables sheet: proceeds only for P8; TSD P3 v3 T2.2 names PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH as package codes for Epic 2.
proposed: Build the match rules as the PAYMENT_MATCH package in rwb-decision and keep the proceeds rows in rwb-payment.

title: S1 owns the valuations but has no table in the Ownership Map
source: TSD S1 v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A against the Ownership Map Tables and Endpoints sheets
description: T3.1 of TSD S1 defines the valuation table as a NEW table of S1, and Architecture v5 slide 41 says rwb-valuation owns the valuations. The Ownership Map Tables sheet lists no table owned by S1 (valuation_ext is P1's), while its Endpoints sheet gives S1 the two valuation paths.
evidence: Ownership Map Endpoints ruling POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations (owner S1, ASM-A6-api-6); Tables sheet: no S1 row; Arch v5 slide 41: rwb-valuation owns the valuations.
proposed: Create rwb_valuation with the valuation and route decision tables of T3.1, and keep valuation_ext with P1 as the SVAF extension table.

title: Eleven business events have no number in the catalogue and three have no contract
source: Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43; per-service AsyncAPI documents of 22 November 2026
description: The numbered catalogue stops at 30, and the plus rows (RouteDecided, AssetSold, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled and Settled, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged, FileDelivered and FileFailed) carry no EV number. ReportPublished (P9), LawsuitFiled (S4), ApprovalDecided (P7) and the two split guarantee events (S3) have no AsyncAPI operation.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 plus rows; asyncapi/rwb-reporting.asyncapi.yaml has no channel; asyncapi/rwb-litigation.asyncapi.yaml has no LawsuitFiled; asyncapi/rwb-guarantee.asyncapi.yaml has one GuaranteeClaim message.
proposed: Number the plus rows EV-31 onwards and add the missing operations to the four AsyncAPI documents.

title: The Arch v5 contract paths and the published OpenAPI files differ
source: Architecture v5 slides 13 to 20 against the per-service OpenAPI files of 22 November 2026
description: The Arch v5 contract slides name operations that the published per-service files do not carry on the same path, for example S1 /cases/{id}/route-proposals against the published POST /cases/{caseId}/route, and P3 /cases/{id}/actions, GET /tasks and GET /case-summary/{id} against the published /me/tasks and PATCH /tasks/{taskId}.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (S1 IN) and slide 14 (P3 IN) against rwb-valuation.yaml and rwb-case.yaml.
proposed: Take the published OpenAPI file as the contract and raise the Arch v5 wording as a correction to the architecture pack.

title: Every module specification is still In review and no approval is recorded
source: Document control of the 20 module specifications of v5
description: All 20 source files carry Status In review. D-RCV-60 has no approval round, so the next version is issued as Draft with the status recorded. This is not a defect of the specification; it is the approval state.
evidence: '| Status | In review |' in every file of the v5 family.
proposed: Record the approval of the v6 family at the design authority and move Status to Approved.

title: No squad is named per service
source: Document control (Build squad) of the v5 family against Template and Rules R5.3
description: Every file names 'TechX recovery squads' as the build squad. Under 19 services the squad per service is not specified, and Template and Rules R5.3 keeps the owner a suggestion only.
evidence: '| Build squad | TechX recovery squads |' in every file of the v5 family.
proposed: Assign a squad per service at the design authority; the suggestion stays TechX for app work and the ACE team for DB work.
